**Serves** {{< meta servings >}} · **Active** {{< meta active-time >}} · **Total** {{< meta total-time >}}

A long, slow rise replaces kneading, and baking in a preheated covered pot traps
steam for a crisp crust. Mix it the night before and bake it the next
afternoon.

## Ingredients

- 400 g (3 cups) bread flour, plus more for dusting
- 8 g (1½ tsp) kosher salt
- 1 g (¼ tsp) instant yeast
- 300 g (1¼ cups) cool water

## Method

1. Stir the flour, salt, and yeast together in a large bowl. Add the water and
   mix with a spoon until no dry flour remains. The dough will be shaggy and
   sticky.
2. Cover and leave at room temperature for 12–18 hr, until the surface is
   dotted with bubbles and the dough has more than doubled.
3. Turn the dough onto a well-floured counter. Fold the edges into the middle a
   few times to form a rough ball, then flip it seam-side down onto a floured
   tea towel or a sheet of parchment.
4. Cover and let rise for 1–2 hr, until a fingerprint springs back slowly.
5. 45 min before baking, put a lidded Dutch oven in the oven and heat to
   450 °F.
6. Tip the dough into the hot pot, seam-side up. Cover and bake for 30 min.
7. Remove the lid and bake another 15–20 min, until the crust is deep brown
   and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
8. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hr before cutting.

## Notes

- If the dough rose on parchment, lower it into the pot on the paper and bake
  it on the paper.
- Up to 100 g of the flour can be whole wheat. Add 15 g (1 tbsp) more water if
  you do.
- In a cold kitchen the first rise can take 18 hr or more. It's ready when the
  surface is covered in bubbles.
